suggestion.title: Redis Public-Facing Service Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly links TeamPCP to 'Redis Attacks' — initial access vector should have been reconstructed. Expects detection for CVE exploitation or unauthenticated Redis protocol abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to TCP 6379 (Redis default) from untrusted IP ranges; flag successful commands without prior authentication handshake; correlate with known Redis RCE payloads (e.g., MODULE LOAD, SCRIPT commands).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redis Authentication Credentials Cached

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for plaintext Redis credentials in process arguments (–requirepass, CONFIG SET password), environment variables, or config files in suspicious locations; correlate with package installation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Modification or Metadata Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Later Supply Chain Campaign'—pipeline should detect repository poisoning, package signing violations, or deployment of modified package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package version downgrades, unsigned or revoked-certificate packages, packages delivered outside normal CI/CD, or hash mismatches against official repositories.

suggestion.title: TeamPCP C2 Infrastructure Communication
suggestion.rationale: Redis compromise is an entry point; article dating back to 2020 suggests persistent C2 infrastructure associated with TeamPCP. Should detect known TeamPCP C2 domains, IPs, or TLS certificates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network egress from Redis-compromised hosts against known TeamPCP OSINT (domain registrations, ASN patterns, certificate CN/SANs); flag anomalous outbound protocols or suspicious TLS renegotiations.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Redis Command Sequence (Lateral Movement)
suggestion.rationale: After Redis compromise, attacker executes reconnaissance and lateral movement. Article timeline (2020+) suggests multi-stage attack; pipeline should detect suspicious Redis KEYS, SCAN, or data exfiltration commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Redis command logs for KEYS *, SCAN 0, AUTH attempts with common/weak credentials, or unexpected DUMP/MIGRATE commands; correlate timing with exploit delivery.

suggestion.title: Malware Dropper via Compromised Redis Data Structure
suggestion.rationale: Redis module loading (MODULE LOAD) or serialized-object deserialization can execute arbitrary code. Supply chain context implies packaged payloads; should detect suspicious binary or script storage in Redis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Redis MODULE LOAD followed by child process spawning; detect unusual script or binary serialization in Redis key-value pairs; correlate with supply chain artifact timestamps.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Suspicious Post-Install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes self-propagating npm worm; worms typically persist via lifecycle scripts. Article body should detail install/postinstall hook execution. No UC generated despite this being core malware behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/uninstall operations preceded by unexpected child processes spawning shell interpreters. Alert on env vars passed to postinstall scripts, especially those accessing secrets or making outbound network calls.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Environment Variable Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states worm 'extracting GitHub Actions runner secrets.' No UC maps credential access from CI/CD secrets. This is the attack's high-value vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes reading GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, or other CI/CD secrets from environment within npm module code paths. Flag data exfiltration via DNS TXT records, base64 in HTTP headers, or blockchain contract calls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Ethereum Smart Contract Interaction from npm Module
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Ethereum smart contracts for C2 routing.' Pipeline generated zero C2 detection. This is anomalous network behavior—npm modules should not initiate blockchain transactions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes making HTTP/HTTPS connections to blockchain RPC endpoints (infura.io, alchemy.com, etherscan.io) or resolving Ethereum contract addresses. Flag payload encoding within contract call parameters (0x... patterns in data field).

suggestion.title: npm Module Self-Propagation via Dependency Graph Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Self-Propagating npm Worm.' Worms must replicate. No UC detects malicious dependency injection or package.json modification during install. This is the propagation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json modifications (additions to dependencies, devDependencies, or version downgrades) and npm registry auth token usage from non-privileged accounts. Flag npm publish operations from compromised package contexts.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from node_modules with Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Worm must execute malicious code post-install. Article provides no specific detection hypothesis, but npm malware signature is child process spawning from node_modules tree with outbound network calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation from node_modules/.bin or node_modules/<package>/lib paths with subsequent DNS/TLS connections to attacker infrastructure. Baseline legitimate package binary usage; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Disclosure in Logs or Temporary Files
suggestion.rationale: If secrets are exfiltrated, they may be staged in logs, environment dumps, or temp files. No UC maps this ex-filtration pattern specific to CI/CD secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm install output logs and temp directories for leaked GitHub tokens (ghp_* patterns), AWS keys, or Ethereum private keys. Cross-reference file modification times against malicious package install timestamps.

suggestion.title: Vishing with Passkey/MFA Update Pretexting
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'UNC6671 operators typically contact employees on their personal mobile phones while spoofing corporate help-desks and claiming that workers need to enroll in passkeys or update their multi-factor authentication settings.' suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound calls claiming to originate from corporate helpdesk (via caller ID spoofing detection) with failed or successful SSO authentication attempts occurring within 30 minutes from unusual geographies. Alert on patterns of employees reporting helpdesk verification calls followed by credential-reset or multi-factor-authentication enrollment events.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing Kit Detection

Flag SSL certificates issued within days for domains impersonating known corporate infrastructure. Correlate failed authentication attempts to legitimate SSO endpoints with proxy traffic to lookalike domains in the same time window.

Detect automated downloads of large numbers of files or calendar/mail objects from OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, or third-party cloud apps within minutes of SSO compromise.

Alert when security notifications or password-reset emails are deleted before being read or within seconds of arrival by a user who shows no prior email deletion patterns.

suggestion.title: Multi-Platform Lateral Movement via Stolen SSO Session Cookies

suggestion.title: Automated Cloud Resource Enumeration Post-SSO Compromise

Detect queries for permissions, roles, and group memberships via Graph API or Okta APIs immediately post-compromise. Flag when a single account queries cloud resource tags or metadata to discover what data is available before exfiltration.

suggestion.title: KVM Guest-to-Host Privilege Escalation via Hypercall
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'privileged L1 guest code escape to Linux hosts' — escape from guest to host kernel requires abnormal hypercall sequences or KVM instruction emulation exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequences of unusual hypercalls from guest VMs, particularly those attempting to access host kernel address space, modify VMCS structures, or trigger unhandled page faults at host privilege level. Alert on nested VM contexts (L1→L2) attempting cross-level escapes.

suggestion.title: KVM Memory-Mapped I/O Escape Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: KVM escapes commonly exploit MMIO mishandling between guest and host; 'Zapscape' likely leverages improper MMIO boundary checking to read/write host kernel memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid or sequential MMIO operations from guest context targeting host-reserved address ranges, or MMIO operations that correlate with subsequent kernel privilege checks being bypassed.

suggestion.title: Host Kernel Code Execution from Guest Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful escape must result in code execution at ring-0; expect kernel panics, privilege escalation syscalls, or unexpected kernel module loads correlating with guest VM activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate guest VM process activity with host kernel panics, BUG() macro triggers, or oops messages. Flag sequences where guest syscalls are immediately followed by root-level code execution on host or unexpected kernel module operations.

suggestion.title: Nested Virtualization L1/L2 Boundary Crossing
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'L1 guest code' — this is nested virtualization. Attacker escapes L1 context to L2 or to host; L1 implies guest-within-guest scenario not typically monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of nested VM configurations where L1 guests attempt to allocate excessive memory, trigger rapid VMEXIT rates, or perform operations inconsistent with normal nested virtualization workloads.

suggestion.title: KVM Kernel Parameter or Data Structure Corruption
suggestion.rationale: Escapes often involve overwriting guest-accessible kernel structures (e.g., modifying KVM pte flags, vCPU state). Article's severity suggests memory corruption vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to kernel virtual address space from guest userspace, or modifications to page table entries via guest-accessible mechanisms. Flag use of mprotect/mmap on /dev/kvm or /dev/mem with CAP_SYS_ADMIN-bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from Model Inference Process

Flag non-standard ports, known malware C2 domains, cloud-storage URLs, or pastebin/Telegram endpoints. Baseline legitimate model-download traffic (PyPI, Hugging Face) and alert on deviations.
